A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Language Guided Skill Discovery (LGSD). Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching content across the changed appendix numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Isaac Gym experiments on Ant locomotion and Franka manipulation, including baseline comparisons, skill trajectories, state coverage, and natural-language goal following.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds downstream Ant task comparisons and an edible-object manipulation demonstration.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 adds a deployment procedure that trains a high-level controller to select skills from a pretrained low-level policy. The original language-distance objective, representation learning, PPO training, and zero-shot skill inference remain. Most Algorithm 1 edits clarify embedding storage and update loops.

E1.justification: v2 adds AntSingleGoal and AntMultiGoal evaluations, including sequential four-goal navigation beyond the existing diversity and zero-shot demonstrations. Figure 1 replaces the colored-cube example with selective manipulation of edible objects among banana, meat can, brick, and mug. The original directional Ant and Franka experiments remain.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain DIAYN, DADS, LSD, CSD, and METRA. All five remain in the manipulation comparisons and are extended to the new downstream tasks; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The new downstream evaluation introduces high-level-controller training, sparse goal rewards, specified goal-sampling ranges, a success radius, and a torso-height termination condition. Table 1 changes Ant observations from 36 to 39 dimensions by adding gravity projection; Table 3 changes the Ant minibatch size from 16384 to 32768. These are reported setting changes, without evidence that retained plots were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 1 replaces the colored-cube case with qualitative evidence that learned skills selectively manipulate edible objects, testing a different semantic constraint. Existing directional-prompt demonstrations and latent-space analyses remain unchanged. No systematic ablation or robustness study is added.

E5.justification: Appendix F.1 newly reports five low-level-controller seeds for the downstream evaluation. Separately, v2 removes Section 5.2's explicit statement that the manipulation results report means and standard deviations over four seeds, although Figure 7 still mentions four runs. This does not establish an increase from four to five runs for the same experiment.

E6.justification: New Figure 9 reports higher downstream rewards and faster learning with LGSD skills than with all five baselines on both Ant tasks. Figure 1 replaces the two-cube results with edible-object selection examples. The retained diversity, directional-control, zero-shot, and latent-space plots have unchanged results.

T1.justification: The language-distance definition, Claim 1, WDM derivation, and pseudometric proof are retained; Appendices A/B become B/C. Pair notation is tidied and feasible-path explanations are expanded, without changing the existing mathematical assumptions or arguments.

C1.justification: The abstract softens 'no existing work directly addresses' semantic diversity to saying it 'remains underexplored.' The introduction's first-work claim and the main contributions concerning diversity, prompt constraints, pseudometric support, and natural-language skill use remain. The downstream experiments mainly strengthen support for retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 acknowledges that specifying prompts for complex tasks can be difficult and presents hierarchical control as an alternative use of learned skills. It hypothesizes that downstream gains arise from focusing on meaningful x/y changes and explains the height cutoff as encouraging walking rather than rolling. Earlier manipulation limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds downstream task and checkpoint-selection details. Algorithm 1 explicitly documents embedding storage and buffer iteration, while observation and minibatch specifications are revised. Existing network architectures, optimizer settings, LLM version, and prompt examples are largely retained; the new reproducibility statement mainly provides pointers.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion remain substantially unchanged. Positioning is modestly refined by the abstract's softened novelty statement and the new explanation of how the downstream setup follows and differs from METRA.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies the skill-inference explanation, expands Section 5.3 into two uses of learned skills, and adds reproducibility and acknowledgment sections. Existing appendix figures receive a dedicated heading. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain, so this is a limited reorganization rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replaced, Figure 9 adds two learning curves, and Table 1 gains an observation row. The ICLR template changes the author block, headers, typography, and placement of some material. Most existing figures and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: v1 supports skill usefulness mainly through diversity measures and qualitative goal-reaching examples. v2 adds comparative downstream learning evaluations on single and sequential Ant goals, with task specifications and repeated-seed information. This substantially strengthens evidence for the central claim that discovered skills are useful beyond diversity itself. Removing Figure 6's explicit uncertainty description weakens reporting, but does not outweigh the added validation.
